Order 
This petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure has been preferred by the accused/petitioner for quashing of FIR dated 13.05.2022 registered at Crime No.27/2022 in Police Station Mahila Thana District Satna for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(n) and 506 of the IPC.
2.

entities.text: Police Station Mahila Thana District Satna
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: According to the prosecution case, on 13.05.2022 the respondent No.2 made a written complaint to the SHO Mahila Thana District Satna against the petitioner stating that the petitioner herein started friendship with her on Facebook in the year 2015 and thereafter, he is said to have committed repeated sexual intercourse upon her against her will with false pretext of marriage between May 2016 to April 2022 and subsequently, he got married elsewhere.

It has also been alleged that the petitioner has threatened her with NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:16259 2 MCRC-47878-2022 dire consequences, if she lodges report to the Police.
Thereafter, on the basis of written complaint dated 13.05.2022, an FIR has been registered against the petitioner herein for offences punishable under Section 376(2)(n) & 506 of the IPC.

Upon lodging of the report by the prosecutrix, investigation was commenced by the Police during the course of which statements of various witnesses including that of the prosecutrix were recorded and other material was collected.
After completion of the investigation charge-sheet has been filed by the Police before the Court concerned.

3. This petition has been preferred by the accused on the ground that the allegations levelled against him by the prosecutrix even if are taken to be true at their face value do not amount to commission of any offence by him.

It is not a case where the accused had developed physical relationship with Krishnakant Pandey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 25 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85257215/
1 the prosecutrix under false pretext of marriage.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is at best a case of breach of promise to marry and cannot be in any manner stretched to be a case of false promise having been made to convince the prosecutrix to engage in sexual relations.
He has further argued that there was no misconception of fact which can be said to have vitiated the consent of the prosecutrix.
The accused is alleged to have committed rape upon the prosecutrix and thereafter, promised to marry her.
However, he allegedly did so for a period of 7 years yet the prosecutrix continued to have physical relationship with him.
She went along with the accused to various places in Satna, Jabalpur and Shahdol, where they had physical relationship hence it cannot be a case of false promise to marry.

It was a simple case of love relationship between the parties, which has gone wrong and is not a case of commission of rape on NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:16259 3 MCRC-47878-2022 false pretext of marriage.
It is further submitted that the proceedings against the accused are gross abuse of the process of law ,hence deserve to be quashed.

Reliance has been placed by the learned counsel for the petitioner on the decision of Apex Court in the case of Dr. Dhruvaram Murlidhar Sonar Vs. State of Maharashtra and others (2019) 18 SCC 191, Pramod Suryabhan Pawar Vs. State of Maharashtra and another (2019) 9 SCC 608, Mandar Deepak Pawar Vs. dated 21.01.2026 and also order passed by this Court in M.Cr.C. No.19761/2023 in Mohammad Sajid Khan Vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh and Ors. dated 16.12.2023.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/State as well as learned counsel for the objector/complainant have strongly opposed the prayer and have submitted that from the allegations as levelled against the accused by the complainant, it is apparent that the same do constitute offence of rape having been committed by him.
The accused firstly promised to marry her then committed rape, which was believed by her.
The consent of the prosecutrix for physical relationship was obtained by the accused by false statement knowing it to be false since the very inception.
It is hence submitted that the petition deserves to be dismissed.

Learned counsel for the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:16259 4 MCRC-47878-2022 complainant further submits that the statements of the prosecutrix has already been recorded before, the trial Court.

He further submits that Section 90 of the IPC may be read as under:-
"A consent is not such a consent as it intended by any section of this Code, if the consent is given by a person under fear of injury, or under a misconception of fact,
and if the person doing the act knows, or has reason to believe, that the consent was given in consequence of such fear or misconception; or Consent of insane person.-- if the consent is given by a person who, from unsoundness of mind, or intoxication, is unable to understand the nature and consequence of that to which he gives his consent; or Consent of child.-- unless the contrary appears from the context, if the consent is given by a person who is under twelve years of age."
6. Learned counsel for the respondent No.2/complainant has placed reliance upon the judgment passed by the Apex Court in the case of Pradeep Kumar Kesharwani Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh &

sentences.text: Another: 2025 SCC Online SC 1947, the Hon'ble Supreme Court highlighted the clear distinction between rape and consensual sexual intercourse.

It was held that where allegations are founded on a promise of marriage, the Court must examine whether the promise was false at its inception and made with a dishonest intention, or whether the relationship was entered into genuinely and failed subsequently.

The relevant observations are as under:-
"13. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties and having gone through the materials on record, we are of the view that the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate committed an error in passing the summoning order.
The High Court too overlooked the relevant aspects of the matter while rejecting the Section 482 application.

It is very apparent on a plain reading of the complaint, more particularly,
considering the nature of the allegations that the same doesn't inspire any confidence.

There is no good explanation NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:16259 5 MCRC-47878-2022 offered, why it took four years for the respondent no.2 to file a complaint.

18. There is a clear distinction between rape and consensual sex and in a case where there is a promise of marriage, the Court must very carefully examine whether the accused had actually wanted to marry the victim, or had mala fide motives and had made a false promise to this effect only to satisfy his lust, as the latter falls in the ambit of cheating or deception."
7.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.

8. The present petition has been filed under Section 482 CrPC seeking quashment of the FIR as well as the criminal proceedings pending before the trial Court on the ground that the allegations arise out of a consensual relationship and that the promise to marry was not false from inception.
9. It is not in dispute that during the course of trial the statement of the prosecutrix has already been recorded before the learned trial Court and she has not turned hostile.

Once the evidence of the prosecutrix has been recorded, this Court, in exercise of inherent jurisdiction under Section 482 CrPC, would not embark upon an appreciation of the evidence to determine its correctness or otherwise, as such exercise falls within the exclusive domain of the trial Court.
The inherent power under Section 482 CrPC is to be exercised sparingly and with great caution, and should not interfere where the matter involves appreciation of evidence.

10. In the present case, since the prosecutrix has already been examined and the trial has progressed, the contentions raised by the petitioner require appreciation of her deposition and other evidence on record, which cannot be undertaken in proceedings under Section 482 CrPC.

At this stage, it cannot be said that the allegations do not disclose any offence or that the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:16259 6 MCRC-47878-2022 continuation of the proceedings would amount to abuse of the process of law.
The petitioner shall be at liberty to raise all permissible grounds before the trial Court, which shall consider the same in accordance with law at the appropriate stage.

Accordingly, this Court is not inclined to exercise inherent powers under Section Krishnakant Pandey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 25 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85257215/
3 482 CrPC.
12.

sentences.text: The petition being devoid of merit is hereby dismissed.

It is made clear that the observations made hereinabove are only for the purpose of deciding the present petition under Section 482 CrPC and are confined to the question as to whether interference in exercise of inherent jurisdiction is warranted or not.
Nothing stated in this order shall be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.

13. The learned trial Court shall proceed with the matter independently and shall decide the case strictly on the basis of the evidence that may come on record, without being influenced in any manner by any observation made in this order.
